review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

3:1.sourceText: Τοῦτο δὲ γίνωσκε, ὅτι ἐν ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις ἐνστήσονται καιροὶ χαλεποί·
3:1.targetText: And know this, that in the last days there will come perilous times,

3:2.sourceText: ἔσονται γὰρ οἱ ἄνθρωποι φίλαυτοι, φιλάργυροι, ἀλαζόνες, ὑπερήφανοι, βλάσφημοι, γονεῦσιν ἀπειθεῖς, ἀχάριστοι, ἀνόσιοι,
3:2.targetText: for men will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boasters, proud, slanderous, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unkind,

groups.note: LSV unkind is an unusual interpretive rendering of the actual ἀνόσιοι, unholy/impious (Thayer, Strong462). The correspondence exposes that underlying Greek head and its difference from the English gloss; it does not assert that unholy ordinarily means unkind or substitute an ordinary kindness noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

3:3.sourceText: ἄστοργοι, ἄσπονδοι, διάβολοι, ἀκρατεῖς, ἀνήμεροι, ἀφιλάγαθοι,
3:3.targetText: without natural affection, implacable, false accusers, without control, barbaric, not lovers of those who are good,

targetPhrases.text: not lovers of those who are good

groups.note: The single compound adjective ἀφιλάγαθοι means not loving good or good people. LSV expands the people construal as not lovers of those who are good; its internal those/who/are words are part of that English compound-adjective rendering, not independent Greek article or be tokens.

3:4.sourceText: προδόται, προπετεῖς, τετυφωμένοι, φιλήδονοι μᾶλλον ἢ φιλόθεοι,
3:4.targetText: traitors, reckless, lofty, lovers of pleasure more than lovers of God,

groups.note: The perfect passive pride/puffing-up participle τετυφωμένοι describes the state of arrogance; LSV renders lofty, not literal physical height.

3:5.sourceText: ἔχοντες μόρφωσιν εὐσεβείας τὴν δὲ δύναμιν αὐτῆς ἠρνημένοι· καὶ τούτους ἀποτρέπου.
3:5.targetText: having a form of piety, but having denied its power; and be turning away from these,

3:6.sourceText: ἐκ τούτων γάρ εἰσιν οἱ ἐνδύνοντες εἰς τὰς οἰκίας καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζοντες γυναικάρια σεσωρευμένα ἁμαρτίαις, ἀγόμενα ἐπιθυμίαις ποικίλαις,
3:6.targetText: for of these there are those coming into the houses and leading captive the weak women, loaded with sins, led away with manifold desires,

groups.note: The diminutive γυναικάρια is rendered weak women as a contextually disparaging designation; the weakness is conveyed by that noun form, without a separate Greek weak adjective. It does not label all women weak.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness article addition: LSV the weak women agrees with TR τὰ γυναικάρια; pinned N1904 gives the anarthrous γυναικάρια.

3:7.sourceText: πάντοτε μανθάνοντα καὶ μηδέποτε εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας ἐλθεῖν δυνάμενα.
3:7.targetText: always learning, and never able to come to a knowledge of truth,

3:8.sourceText: ὃν τρόπον δὲ Ἰάννης καὶ Ἰαμβρῆς ἀντέστησαν Μωϋσεῖ, οὕτως καὶ οὗτοι ἀνθίστανται τῇ ἀληθείᾳ, ἄνθρωποι κατεφθαρμένοι τὸν νοῦν, ἀδόκιμοι περὶ τὴν πίστιν.
3:8.targetText: and even as Jannes and Jambres stood against Moses, so these also stand against the truth, men corrupted in mind, disapproved concerning the faith;

groups.note: The ὃν τρόπον expression means in the manner that/just as; LSV even as renders the whole comparison without separate Greek even or manner nouns in English.
The accusative mind phrase marks the respect of corruption, rendered in mind without a separately written Greek in preposition.

3:9.targetText: but they will not advance any further, for their folly will be evident to all, as theirs also became.

3:11.sourceText: τοῖς διωγμοῖς, τοῖς παθήμασιν, οἷά μοι ἐγένετο ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ, ἐν Ἰκονίῳ, ἐν Λύστροις· οἵους διωγμοὺς ὑπήνεγκα, καὶ ἐκ πάντων με ἐρύσατο ὁ Κύριος.
3:11.targetText: the persecutions, the afflictions, that befell me in Antioch, in Iconium, in Lystra; what persecutions I endured! And the LORD delivered me out of all.

3:12.sourceText: καὶ πάντες δὲ οἱ θέλοντες ζῆν εὐσεβῶς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ διωχθήσονται.
3:12.targetText: And all who will to live piously in Christ Jesus will also be persecuted,

groups.note: Greek καί inclusively qualifies all at the front of the clause; LSV places also with will be persecuted. The additive particle is retained with this English scope/order difference explicit; δέ supplies initial And.

3:13.sourceText: πονηροὶ δὲ ἄνθρωποι καὶ γόητες προκόψουσιν ἐπὶ τὸ χεῖρον, πλανῶντες καὶ πλανώμενοι.
3:13.targetText: and evil men and impostors will advance to the worse, leading astray and being led astray.

3:14.sourceText: σὺ δὲ μένε ἐν οἷς ἔμαθες καὶ ἐπιστώθης, εἰδὼς παρὰ τίνων ἔμαθες,
3:14.targetText: And you—remain in the things which you learned and were entrusted with, having known from whom you learned,

groups.note: LSV were entrusted with is an interpretive wording for the actual πιστόω passive ἐπιστώθης; N1904 and TR both have that verb. Thayer at this verse gives were firmly persuaded/assured of, a conviction about learned teaching, not the different verb πιστεύω meaning entrust. This exposes the actual underlying head and the assurance-versus-entrusting role difference, without teaching those as general interchangeable senses.
N1904 τίνων is plural from whom, whereas TR τίνος is singular. English whom does not distinguish the number; this link preserves the pinned plural source identity.

3:15.sourceText: καὶ ὅτι ἀπὸ βρέφους ἱερὰ γράμματα οἶδας, τὰ δυνάμενά σε σοφίσαι εἰς σωτηρίαν διὰ πίστεως τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
3:15.targetText: and because you have known the Holy Writings from infancy, which are able to make you wise—to salvation, through faith that [is] in Christ Jesus.

unmappedTarget.reason: English the Holy Writings uses an explicit determiner, also written in TR τὰ ἱερὰ γράμματα; pinned N1904’s initial Holy Writings phrase is anarthrous. The later actual τὰ introduces which and is not exchanged with this first article.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

3:16.targetText: Every Writing [is] God-breathed, and profitable for teaching, for conviction, for correction, for instruction that [is] in righteousness,

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

review.note: The Greek line is verbless. LSV explicitly supplies the first is to predicate God-breathed and profitable of Every Writing, and the second is in the article-plus-in-righteousness modifier. Neither copula is assigned to a bare Greek article, and this records the displayed construction without resolving alternative syntactic analyses for other translations.
